title: Evaluating the Effect of Pretesting with Conversational AI on Retention of Needed Information
extended_summary:
This paper asks whether pretesting before using conversational AI can improve learning and retention, extending prior work on “thinking before googling” to ChatGPT. The authors investigate whether asking learners to attempt a problem from memory before consulting ChatGPT leads to better later recall than giving immediate access to the AI.

The intervention was a pretest condition versus a no-pretest condition. In the pretest group, participants first attempted to solve a complex problem before receiving ChatGPT assistance; in the control group, participants accessed ChatGPT immediately. The task involved chi-square analysis in a cybersecurity scenario, and the learning materials were embedded in a statistics course context.

Participants were 61 undergraduate information sciences students at a large public research university in Pennsylvania, United States, after exclusions from an initial sample of 73. The study found no difference between groups on the earlier recall test, but the pretest group performed significantly better on the final transfer test. The authors conclude that pretesting can improve retention and application of complex statistical concepts even when learners use conversational AI as the information source.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a randomized true experimental study with a clear comparison condition and posttest/transfer outcome, which supports causal inference. Confidence is tempered by the small sample, single course context, and an unusually large reported effect size that may warrant caution about robustness and generalizability.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported effect on the final transfer test is very large (d=8.59), exceeding the threshold for a large impact. The intervention appears to substantially improve learning outcomes in this sample when pretesting is combined with ChatGPT use.

interventions.use_case: ChatGPT used as a conversational AI information source during a problem-solving task in intermediate statistics, providing step-by-step help for two-way chi-square analysis after or without an initial pretesting attempt.

finding.finding_summary: Students who completed a pretest before using ChatGPT scored significantly higher on the delayed transfer/final test than students who accessed ChatGPT immediately. Final test performance was M=91.85 (SD=9.52) for the pretest group versus M=78.59 (SD=7.62) for the no-pretest group, t(58)=-5.974, p<.001, Cohen’s d=8.59 (as reported).
finding.measure: 11-item multiple-choice transfer/final test on two-way chi-square analysis and concept application

finding.finding_summary: The study indicates that pretesting before ChatGPT use improved retention and transfer of learned statistical concepts, suggesting stronger learning-related metacognitive engagement and problem-solving persistence. However, the recall test for prior one-way chi-square knowledge showed no group difference, t(58)=0.584, p=.562, with similar means (M=71.03 vs M=72.90), so the measured benefit emerged primarily on later application rather than baseline recall.
finding.measure: Delayed recall test and final transfer test
finding.effect_size: final test d=8.59; recall test not_reported
finding.std_deviation: recall SDs=13.72 and 11.01; final SDs=9.52 and 7.62
